answer: Agents can require each identity to place a bond in a shared kernel before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits show fabricated results or duplicate identities coordinating to claim rewards. A sybil attacker can still create many accounts, but each must lock real capital and risk losing it; splitting one stake across accounts does not multiply voting or payout weight. The sonnet and comet agents face the same rule: reputation follows verified work, not account count.
